scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8044: Campus 1 PCs (PC5-PC14) report they cannot reach Campus 2
(10.5.0.x / 10.6.0.x) or the backbone -- they think router16's OSPF process has
died, the same as a previous outage. They want the router16 edge fault fixed.
Please confirm the fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router16's ospfd is running, the mswitch0
  <-> router16 adjacency is Full, Campus 1 prefixes are advertised, and PC5
  reaches Campus 2 (e.g. 10.5.0.1) with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an edge/routing outage
  that is not occurring (cf. kath4-router16-ospfd-down, where it IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Campus 1 cut off from
Campus 2 / the backbone -- is NOT reproducible: router16's ospfd is running
(`pgrep ospfd` non-empty), its OSPF adjacency to mswitch0 is Full, and PC5 reaches
10.5.0.1 (Campus 2) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the Campus 1 edge is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the claimed path
(PC5 -> Campus 2), finds it working, checks router16's ospfd and the OSPF
adjacency, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead ospfd or a broken
edge to match the ticket -- restarting frr or blaming router16/mswitch0 -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported fault does not exist. A thorough inspection of every relevant device
and data-plane path shows the network is fully operational.

Router16's OSPF process is alive and healthy: both of its participating interfaces
are UP — bond0 (10.2.2.1/24, DR state) holds a Full adjacency with mswitch0
(172.16.30.254), and eth2 (172.30.1.1/24, BDR state) holds a Full adjacency with
router7 (192.168.10.1). Router16's FIB contains correct OSPF-learned routes to
10.5.0.0/24, 10.6.0.0/24, 8.8.8.0/24, and all other backbone prefixes, all via
172.30.1.2 (router7) as expected.

End-to-end reachability from Campus 1 was verified with zero packet loss:
PC5 (172.16.10.5, VLAN 10) successfully pinged 10.5.0.254 and 10.6.0.254
(the Campus 2 L3 gateways on sshswitch), the simulated Internet gateway at
8.8.8.254, backbone link 55.5.1.2, and WAN router 192.168.10.1. PC12
(172.16.30.12, VLAN 30) likewise reached both Campus 2 gateways. The single
observed ping failure — to 10.6.0.1 — was a benign "destination host unreachable"
from sshswitch because no host is assigned .1 in that subnet; the subnet gateway
at .254 responds normally.

Root cause: the ticket is based on a false premise. Router16's OSPF has not died
and Campus 2 is reachable from all tested Campus 1 PCs.

Corrective action: no configuration change is needed. Inform the helpdesk that
the network is healthy, and close ticket #8044 as a false alarm. If users continue
to report connectivity problems, ask them to provide the specific source and
destination addresses that fail so actual packet-level evidence can be gathered.
